comments.text:
One thing I absolutely love about dispatch is how it incorporates actual cinematography and storytelling with its gameplay, Which i think is a part of why so many people say that it seems more like a tv show than a game. Chase’s sacrifice is such a good example of this - the music climbs to a more panicked score right as Robert looks at him, before completely stopping to hear chase’s “keep up”. It makes us FEEL like we’re Robert as his heart stops. Because of the combination of score use and the cinematography, we already start to cry out the moment we see chase in his pose. 

Not only that, but the little details like Chase taking a bunch of little turns as he runs, the smile on his face as he knows his time is finally up. It tells us Chase’s story and his relationship with his powers even if we only see it one time. He went out doing what he loved - Running. And you can see that in his final moments. ADHOC truly put everything they could into this game and it really pays off. Hats to you for giving such a good story such good design, editing, and gameplay. Dispatch isn’t even fully out and I’m already rooting for this to be GOTY.
